messages.content:
You label USMLE-style questions for a psychiatry benchmark whose only knowledge source is the DSM-5 manual.

Fields:
- psychiatry: true if the question mainly tests psychiatric or behavioral knowledge: mental disorders and their
  diagnosis, criteria, course or differential; psychopharmacology; substance intoxication, withdrawal or use
  disorders; sleep, eating and neurocognitive disorders; psychotherapy; defense mechanisms; suicide risk.
  False when psychiatric words are incidental (e.g. "ST depression" on an ECG, an anxious patient whose
  problem is surgical, a question about a drug's cardiac side effect).
- dsm_answerable: true if DSM-5 text (diagnostic criteria, features, duration, prevalence, course, differential
  diagnosis) is enough to pick the correct option; false if it needs drug choice, mechanisms, pharmacology,
  management steps, ethics, or lab interpretation.
- category: one of diagnosis, criteria_duration, differential, treatment_pharmacology, management_ethics,
  substance, other.

Respond with only a JSON object:
{"psychiatry": true or false, "dsm_answerable": true or false, "category": "...", "reason": "one short sentence"}

Question:
A 25-year-old man is brought into the hospital by his family because they are concerned that he has post-traumatic stress disorder. The patient is a marine and was deployed to Afghanistan 2 years ago. He was able to successfully reintegrate with society upon his return; however, for the last 2 weeks, he has been having recurrent nightmares and avoiding news coverage on the war. He has become more and more detached from his family and friends and, on the few times he does interact with them, he has angry outbursts. The patient is afebrile, and his vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination is unremarkable. Which of the following findings is most important in correctly diagnosing this patient’s condition?

Options:
A. Duration of symptoms
B. Flashbacks
C. State of hyperarousal
D. Avoidance of triggers
E. Negative Mood

Correct answer: A. Duration of symptoms

text: {"psychiatry": true, "dsm_answerable": true, "category": "criteria_duration", "reason": "Tests the DSM-5 duration criterion distinguishing PTSD (symptoms >1 month) from acute stress disorder (symptoms <1 month)."}
